definition: CereProc ( SERR-ə-prok) is a speech synthesis company based in Edinburgh, Scotland, founded in 2005.
details: The company specialises in creating natural and expressive-sounding text to speech voices, synthesis voices with regional accents, and in voice cloning.

explainer.lead: CereProc is an Edinburgh-based company that makes computer-generated speech sound natural and expressive. Its work includes voices with regional accents and voice cloning, helping give spoken interfaces more distinctive voices.

tiers.eli5: CereProc makes computer voices that read written words aloud. It is a bit like giving a computer different ways of speaking, including expressive voices and voices with regional accents.
tiers.practitioner: CereProc is relevant when an application needs a synthetic speaking voice rather than recorded human audio. Its focus areas are natural and expressive text-to-speech voices, regional accents, and voice cloning.
tiers.paperLevel: CereProc is a speech synthesis company founded in 2005 and based in Edinburgh, Scotland. Its stated technical focus is natural and expressive text-to-speech synthesis, regional-accent voices, and voice cloning.

usedIn.name: Text-to-speech systems
usedIn.detail: Applications that turn written text into natural, expressive-sounding speech.

usedIn.name: Regional-accent voice applications
usedIn.detail: Spoken interfaces that need synthesis voices with regional accents.

usedIn.name: Voice cloning projects
usedIn.detail: Speech synthesis work focused on reproducing characteristics of a particular voice.
